title: Choose Squint's new look
question: The roll picked Galley Proof. Keep it, take the other card, or re-roll.

options.label: Galley Proof
options.lineage: a copy editor's marked-up galley, blue pencil and margin queries
options.thesis: Squint marks writing the way an editor marks a proof: queries in the margin, never a stamp on the page.
options.viewport: A blue-pencil top rail, then the text itself as a wide galley with a margin column; after a check the verdict is the editor's note in large type and flagged passages get a bracket in the margin.
options.risk: Turns into a paper costume if the margin marks get decorative instead of carrying the evidence.

raised.raise: One region owns each state: the galley is the screen, before and after a check.
One reserved colour rides above the marks: only the word in focus gets the ink box.
Progress writes itself onto the page as margin notes instead of a separate status panel.
One size does the work: a single reading size for the text, two sizes for everything else.
Numbers sit in one tight tabular column instead of sentences around every figure.

options.label: Graded Paper
options.lineage: a teacher's marked essay handed back
options.thesis: The result comes back like a marked essay: the reading in the top corner, notes down the margin.
options.viewport: Composer as a ruled sheet; after a check the band sits as a corner mark and notes run in the margin.
options.risk: Familiar, and a red-pen grade reads as judging the writer, which Squint must never do.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Every area a swelling lobe of flat colour.
options.viewport: One green lobe holding the composer.
options.risk: Playful map shapes fight a tool about honest evidence.
options.case: Loses both axes: nobody checking an essay thinks in maps.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed colour language with one course colour above.
options.viewport: Text as terrain, purple course over flagged passages.
options.case: Loses both axes: clever, but writers don't read maps.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the item in focus.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each step stamps itself onto a coupon.
options.viewport: The check as a coupon book.
options.case: Loses both axes: travel ephemera has nothing to do with writing.
options.kept: States write onto the object; nothing pops up elsewhere.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: Tabbed section boards under acetate leaves.
options.viewport: Composer on an acetate leaf over a coloured board.
options.risk: Heavy material for a one-box tool.
options.case: Loses both axes: too much world for one text box.
options.kept: One reading size does the work.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A pixel wordmark over dense columns.
options.risk: Pixel type hurts reading the user's own words.
options.case: Loses both axes: it would read as a retro stunt.
options.kept: The lens repeats the word at specimen scale.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Barcode columns in pure black and white.
options.risk: Cold, and strobing is wrong for anxious people.
options.case: Loses both axes: machine aesthetic on a tool about people.
options.kept: Numbers in one tight tabular column.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What AI detectors ship, done properly: a clean white card and a big percentage.
canonCard.viewport: A big text box, a big percentage gauge, highlighted sentences.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other detector, which is the AI-sloppy feel you want gone.
